NAME: Cluster expansion
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: A cluster expansion fitted to 333 DFT‑computed LiCoO₂ configurations using a genetic‑algorithm‑guided sparse regression achieves a root‑mean‑square error of 2.49 meV per primitive cell under 10‑fold cross‑validation and accurately reproduces formation energies, especially for configurations on or near the convex hull.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The atomic cluster expansion (ACE) is generalized to model scalar, vectorial and tensorial atomic properties and to include additional atomic degrees of freedom—species, magnetic moments, and charges—on equal footing with atomic positions.
ARTICLE: Bridging scales with Machine Learning: From first principles statistical mechanics to continuum phase field computations to study order-disorder transitions in LixCoO2

NAME: Atomic Cluster Expansion extended to scalar, vectorial, tensorial properties with magnetic moments and charge transfer
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The atomic cluster expansion (ACE) is generalized to model scalar, vectorial and tensorial atomic properties and to include additional atomic degrees of freedom—species, magnetic moments, and charges—on equal footing with atomic positions.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The derived ACE formulas enable efficient evaluation of forces and magnetic torques.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: At the lowest order, the magnetic ACE reproduces a distance‑dependent Heisenberg interaction.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Representing tensors with spherical harmonics yields a dramatically sparser basis, where a rank‑N Cartesian tensor with 3^N components can be represented by (N+1)^2 spherical harmonics (e.g., a 10th‑order tensor requires 121 harmonics instead of 59 049 Cartesian components).
ARTICLE: Atomic cluster expansion of scalar, vectorial and tensorial properties and including magnetism and charge transfer
OTHER: Atomic Cluster Expansion

NAME: Graph Neural Network for atomic property prediction in defective crystalline solids
TYPE: method
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The GNN predicts atomic von Mises stress in polycrystalline graphene with a mean normalized relative error of 5.5% and a maximum error below 7% on a test set of 400 crystals.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The GNN predicts atomic tensile stress in porous graphene membranes under tensile strain with a mean normalized relative error of 4.9% and a maximum error of about 10%.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The GNN reproduces the linear decrease of Young’s modulus with vacancy concentration in porous graphene, matching MD results and yielding the fitted relation E = 823.7 − 5635.6·Cv (GPa).

DIRECT_CLAIMS: In polycrystalline aluminum, the GNN predicts atomic potential energy with a mean normalized relative error of 11.0% (maximum ≈13%) and achieves R² = 0.99 for mean potential energy versus grain number.
DATASET_METRIC: Polycrystalline graphene
DATASET_METRIC: Porous graphene membranes
ARTICLE: Linking atomic structural defects to mesoscale properties in crystalline solids using graph neural networks

NAME: convex hull
TYPE: method
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Training on OMat24 results in models with better extrapolation to regions with lower dataset density farther away from the convex hull compared to models trained on other datasets.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: A cluster expansion fitted to 333 DFT‑computed LiCoO₂ configurations using a genetic‑algorithm‑guided sparse regression achieves a root‑mean‑square error of 2.49 meV per primitive cell under 10‑fold cross‑validation and accurately reproduces formation energies, especially for configurations on or near the convex hull.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: CGAT-2 network achieves a mean absolute test error of 21 meV/atom for distance to the convex hull, enabling prediction of thermodynamic stability from unrelaxed crystal structures.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The ML-assisted high-throughput search uncovered 19,512 additional materials on the convex hull of thermodynamic stability after DFT validation.
ARTICLE: AFLOW: an automatic framework for high-throughput materials discovery
